mainTopic: עיקור סימנין in a bird, זעירי's ruling on a broken neck bone, and the מצוה of הבדלה in a bird עולה
overview: This amud deals with three questions about bird שחיטה and מליקה. First, it asks how far רמי בר יחזקאל's rule, that עיקור סימנין does not disqualify a bird, reaches. One view ties the rule to the opinion that bird שחיטה is only מדברי סופרים. רב אשי argues the reverse: under the rabbinic view, bird שחיטה copies animal שחיטה completely, so עיקור should apply. רבין בר קיסי limits the rule a different way, to מליקה only, and the גמרא admits this disagrees with שמואל. Next, זעירי rules that a broken neck bone with most of the flesh makes an animal or bird a נבלה. רב חסדא tries to prove this from a bird pinched with a knife, but the proof is rejected, because pinching with a knife is not slaughter at all, whether due to מחליד or דורס. Finally, רבא challenges זעירי: if a broken neck makes a נבלה, why does the כהן keep pinching a bird that is already dead? This leads to a discussion of the מצוה of הבדלה in a bird עולה, which ends with the rule that whatever is part of שחיטה is part of הבדלה.

steps.title: If bird slaughter is from the Torah, ripping does disqualify
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the opening statement: according to the view that bird שחיטה is from the Torah, עיקור does disqualify a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says bird slaughter is from the Torah, ripping out the סימנים does disqualify.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement that began just before this section. It limits רמי בר יחזקאל's rule, "there is no עיקור in a bird," to only one opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that if bird שחיטה is a Torah law, it has all the strict rules of animal שחיטה, including עיקור. So רמי בר יחזקאל's lenient rule would only work for the view that bird שחיטה is rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Ripping or tearing the סימנים (windpipe and food pipe) out of their place, which can disqualify a שחיטה
Ritual slaughter of a bird
From the Torah itself, a Torah-level law

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
there is slaughter for a bird from the Torah,
there is ripping (it disqualifies).

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל לְמַאן דְּאָמַר יֵשׁ שְׁחִיטָה לָעוֹף מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a limiting statement on רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching that began just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Under the view that bird שחיטה is from the Torah, עיקור disqualifies a bird.

steps.title: The opposite makes more sense for the Torah-law view
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the opposite is more logical: under the Torah-law view, the oral teaching might have said there is no עיקור in a bird.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: On the contrary, the opposite makes sense! According to the one who says bird slaughter is from the Torah, we can say that this is how God taught משה: that there is no ripping. And even according to the one who says a bird is like an animal, when it comes to ripping it would not be like an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects the previous statement and argues the reverse. Under the Torah-law view, bird שחיטה rules come from a special teaching, and that teaching could have left out עיקור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If bird שחיטה is from the Torah, its details were taught directly to משה, so the teaching itself can set its own rules. Even if the Torah-law view generally compares a bird to an animal, it could make an exception for עיקור.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
The opposite is more logical
He taught him (God taught משה orally)
Like an animal: bird שחיטה follows the rules of animal שחיטה

phrases.english: He said to him: On the contrary,
phrases.notes: The one speaking here is רב אשי.

phrases.english: the opposite makes sense!
According to the one who says there is slaughter
for a bird from the Torah,
one can say that this is how He taught him,
phrases.notes: "He taught him" means God taught משה the details of bird slaughter by mouth.

phrases.english: that there is no ripping.
And even according to the one who says it is like an animal,
regarding the matter of ripping
it would not be like an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 1 by flipping its logic.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the Torah-law view must include עיקור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A Torah-level oral teaching can define its own details, so it could leave out עיקור even if a bird is otherwise like an animal.
steps.confusionAlert: You might expect the Torah-law view to be the stricter one. רב אשי's point is that a Torah teaching can set its own exceptions, so it may actually be more lenient here.

steps.title: The rabbinic view copies animal slaughter completely
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי finishes his argument: under the rabbinic view, bird שחיטה is learned from an animal, so every rule, including עיקור, is the same as an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says there is no bird slaughter from the Torah, only by rabbinic law, where do they learn it from? From an animal. So the whole matter is like an animal!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי finishes his reversal. Under the rabbinic view, the Rabbis modeled bird שחיטה completely on animal שחיטה, so עיקור should disqualify a bird too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no separate teaching for birds under this view; the only source is animal שחיטה. With nothing special to make an exception, every animal rule carries over. So רמי בר יחזקאל's lenient rule fits the rabbinic view worst, which is the opposite of what step 1 said.

keyTerms.meaning: By rabbinic law, from the words of the Sages
They learn it from (a source)
The entire matter, every detail

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי: under the Torah-law view an oral teaching could exempt birds from עיקור, but under the rabbinic view birds copy animals exactly, so עיקור would apply.

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
there is no slaughter for a bird from the Torah
but only by rabbinic law,
from where do they learn it? From an animal,
so the whole matter is like an animal!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר: אֵין שְׁחִיטָה לָעוֹף מִן הַתּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב אשי's reversal by explaining the other side.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that the rabbinic view would have no עיקור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The rabbinic view's only source is animal שחיטה, so it has no basis to drop עיקור.

steps.title: A different limit: no ripping problem in pinching, but yes in slaughter
steps.stepSummary: רבינא quotes רבין בר קיסי, who limits רמי בר יחזקאל's rule to מליקה; in שחיטה, עיקור does disqualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: רבין בר קיסי told me: What רמי בר יחזקאל taught, that there is no ripping of סימנים in a bird, was said only about pinching, but in slaughter there is ripping.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new way to limit רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching. Instead of splitting by Torah law versus rabbinic law, it splits by the method: מליקה versus שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מליקה is pinching the neck of a bird offering from the back. According to רבין בר קיסי, the lenient rule about עיקור applies only there, and a regular שחיטה of a bird is disqualified by עיקור just like an animal.

keyTerms.meaning: The two signs: windpipe and food pipe, which must be cut in שחיטה
Pinching: killing a bird offering by cutting through the back of the neck with the fingernail
We said this only (in a certain case): a limiting formula

phrases.english: Ravina said,
Ravin bar Kisi said to me:
That which Rami bar Yechezkel teaches,
there is no ripping of the simanim in a bird,
we said it only regarding pinching,
but regarding slaughter, there is ripping.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא, אָמַר לִי רָבִין בַּר קִיסִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different way to limit רמי בר יחזקאל's teaching instead of the Torah/rabbinic split.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no עיקור problem in מליקה, but there is in שחיטה.

steps.title: Challenge: שמואל says pinching matches slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבין בר קיסי from שמואל's rule that whatever is valid or invalid in שחיטה is the same in מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי ירמיה say in the name of שמואל: Whatever is valid in slaughter, its matching spot on the back of the neck is valid in pinching; so whatever is invalid in slaughter is invalid in pinching!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבין בר קיסי's split. According to שמואל, שחיטה and מליקה follow the same rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says the rules of מליקה at the back mirror the rules of שחיטה at the front. If עיקור disqualifies שחיטה, it should also disqualify מליקה. That contradicts רבין בר קיסי, who said מליקה has no עיקור problem.

keyTerms.meaning: Opposite it, the matching spot
The back of the neck, where מליקה is done
Valid
Invalid, disqualified

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yirmeya say that Shmuel said:
Whatever is valid for slaughter
its matching spot on the back of the neck is valid for pinching,
so what is invalid there is invalid here!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the split between מליקה and שחיטה made in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין בר קיסי's claim that עיקור disqualifies שחיטה but not מליקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל makes the rules of מליקה match the rules of שחיטה, so the two cannot differ about עיקור.

steps.title: Answer: this view disagrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבין בר קיסי's teaching simply disagrees with שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not reconcile the two teachings. It admits that רבין בר קיסי's view and שמואל's rule are a real disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of explaining away the contradiction, the גמרא accepts it. רבין בר קיסי holds that מליקה and שחיטה can differ about עיקור, which goes against שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees: the two teachings are a real dispute

steps.whatToRemember: רבין בר קיסי limits "no עיקור in a bird" to מליקה. This goes against שמואל's rule that מליקה mirrors שחיטה, and the גמרא accepts that they disagree.

phrases.english: That one disagrees.
phrases.notes: "That one" is רבין בר קיסי's teaching; it disagrees with שמואל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 5 by admitting a real dispute.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Admitting a real dispute: the teaching disagrees with שמואל
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבין בר קיסי's split must fit with שמואל's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבין בר קיסי holds against שמואל, so there is no contradiction to resolve.

steps.title: A broken neck bone with most of the flesh makes it a carcass
steps.stepSummary: זעירי rules that if the neck bone breaks along with most of the surrounding flesh, the animal or bird is a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: זעירי said: If the neck bone broke and most of the flesh went with it, it is a נבלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule from זעירי about a broken neck bone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: זעירי is not saying the animal is only a טרפה, meaning wounded and forbidden but still able to be slaughtered. He says it counts as already dead, a נבלה, so שחיטה can no longer help it.

keyTerms.meaning: The neck bone (the spine at the neck)
An animal that died without a valid שחיטה; it is forbidden to eat and gives off טומאה
Most of the flesh around the bone

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up נבלה with טרפה. A טרפה is fatally wounded but still alive, so שחיטה protects it from נבלה impurity. A נבלה is already treated as dead.

phrases.english: Ze'eiri said:
If the neck bone was broken
and most of the flesh along with it,
it is a carcass.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of עיקור.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A broken neck bone together with most of the surrounding flesh gives the status of נבלה, not just טרפה.

steps.title: Proof from a bird offering pinched with a knife
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא supports זעירי from a משנה: a bird pinched with a knife still makes clothes טמא, so a broken neck must count as a נבלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: We also learned this in a משנה. If someone pinched a bird with a knife, it makes clothes טמא when it is in the throat. If you say a broken neck only makes it a טרפה, then since for this bird pinching counts as its slaughter, the knife should at least save it from נבלה impurity.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא brings a proof from a משנה to back up זעירי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pinching from the back of the neck breaks the neck bone. If that only made the bird a טרפה, the pinching would act like a שחיטה and protect it from נבלה impurity. Since the משנה says it still carries נבלה impurity, a broken neck must make it a נבלה.

keyTerms.meaning: He pinched: killing a bird offering by cutting from the back of the neck
Makes the clothes of someone who swallows it טמא while it is in his throat; this is the special טומאה of a kosher bird that is a נבלה
A fatally wounded animal; forbidden to eat, but a valid שחיטה keeps it from being a נבלה
To make it free of נבלה impurity

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
We too have learned this in a mishna:
If one pinched with a knife,
it makes garments impure when in the throat.
And if you say it is only a tereifa,
phrases.notes: He means the bird whose neck bone was broken by the pinching.

phrases.english: then since its pinching is its slaughter,
let the knife be effective for it
to free it from carcass impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports זעירי's rule from a משנה.
steps.raayaObject: זעירי's rule that a broken neck bone with most of the flesh makes it a נבלה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in זבחים: a bird offering pinched with a knife still carries נבלה impurity in the throat.

steps.title: Pinching with a knife is not slaughter at all
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the knife fails there because pinching with a knife is not a valid slaughter at all, not because of the broken neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: There, the reason is that it is not a slaughter at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב חסדא's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא assumed pinching with a knife is a valid slaughter that should protect a טרפה. The גמרא answers that pinching with a knife does not count as slaughter in the first place. So the משנה tells us nothing about whether a broken neck makes a bird a נבלה or a טרפה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not a slaughter at all

phrases.english: They say: There,
it is because it is not slaughter at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: הָתָם מִשּׁוּם דְּלָאו שְׁחִיטָה הִיא כְּלָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only רב חסדא's proof is rejected; זעירי's rule itself is not disproven.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof wrongly assumed that pinching with a knife counts as a valid slaughter.

steps.title: Why is pinching with a knife invalid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why pinching with a knife does not count as slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the last step. This short question sets up the two answers that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said pinching with a knife is not slaughter at all, but it did not say why. The גמרא now wants that reason spelled out.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rejection in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a knife-pinching does not count as slaughter at all.

steps.title: Two reasons: hiding the knife or pressing it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the knife is hidden while cutting (מחליד). רבא says the knife is pressed instead of drawn (דורס).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: Because he hides the knife. רבא said: Because he presses the knife.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים each give a different reason why pinching with a knife is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both מחליד and דורס are known problems that disqualify a שחיטה. רב הונא points to the knife being covered while it cuts. רבא points to the knife being pushed down instead of being drawn across.

keyTerms.meaning: Hiding the knife: the blade is covered while it cuts
Pressing: pushing the knife down instead of drawing it back and forth

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
Because he conceals the knife.
Rava said:
Because he presses the knife.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הוּנָא אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַחְלִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא: the knife is hidden (מחליד). רבא: the knife is pressed (דורס).

steps.title: Why doesn't רב הונא say pressing?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב הונא did not use רבא's reason of pressing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'because he hides it': why doesn't he say 'because he presses'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב הונא did not give רבא's reason. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pressing seems like an obvious problem with a knife, so the גמרא wants to know why רב הונא needed a different reason.

phrases.english: The one who says: Because he conceals,
what is the reason he does not say
because he presses?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַחְלִיד, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹרֵס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at רב הונא's opinion from step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב הונא rejects דורס as the reason.

steps.title: רב הונא allows back-and-forth in pinching
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא holds that drawing back and forth in מליקה is valid, so pressing is not his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that drawing back and forth in pinching is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב הונא does not use the reason of pressing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הונא's view, מליקה done by drawing back and forth is valid. So the way the knife moves is not the problem for him. The problem must be something else: the knife being hidden.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds (this is his view)
Drawing back and forth

phrases.english: He holds:
Drawing back and forth in pinching is valid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב הונא holds that back-and-forth movement in מליקה is valid, so דורס is not his reason.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבא say hiding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא did not use רב הונא's reason of hiding the knife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who says 'because he presses': why doesn't he say 'because he hides it'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question about רבא. This sets up the final explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the question goes the other way: why did רבא not accept רב הונא's reason of מחליד?

phrases.english: And the one who says: Because he presses,
what is the reason he does not say
because he conceals?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא דּוֹרֵס, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מַחְלִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the same kind of question as step 12, this time about רבא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבא rejects מחליד as the reason.

steps.title: Hiding means covered, but here the knife is exposed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains on רבא's behalf ("he would tell you") that חלדה means the knife is covered, like a rat hidden under a house. When cutting from the back of the neck, the knife stays exposed.
steps.simpleTranslation: He would tell you: What does hiding look like? Like a rat living in the hidden foundations of houses. Here, the knife is exposed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבא does not use the reason of hiding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חלדה comes from חולדה, a rat that lives hidden under houses. So it only applies when the blade is covered. When pinching with a knife from the back of the neck, the blade can be seen, so the only problem left is pressing.

keyTerms.meaning: Hiding the blade under flesh or skin while cutting
A rat or weasel
It is exposed (it can be seen)

steps.whatToRemember: Pinching with a knife is not a valid slaughter. רב הונא says the problem is מחליד; רבא says it is דורס, because the blade stays exposed and is not truly hidden. Because of this, רב חסדא's proof for זעירי falls away.

phrases.english: He would say to you:
What does concealing look like?
Like a rat living in the foundations of houses
that are covered over.
Here, the knife is exposed.
phrases.notes: Here means pinching with a knife from the back of the neck, where the blade stays out in the open.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: חלדה only applies when the blade is covered; in pinching with a knife the blade is exposed.

steps.title: רבא asks why one keeps pinching a dead bird
steps.stepSummary: רבא says that if the earlier ruling bothers him, his real difficulty is this: once the neck bone and most of the flesh are cut in מליקה, the bird is dead, so why keep pinching?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If something bothers me, this is what bothers me: Does he really stand and pinch a dead bird?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא returns to זעירי's ruling in step 7 and challenges it. If a broken neck bone with most of the flesh makes a bird a נבלה, then in מליקה the bird is already dead before the סימנים are reached, so what does the rest of the pinching accomplish?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מליקה the כהן cuts from the back of the neck, through the bone and most of the flesh, before he reaches the סימנים. By the ruling that a broken neck bone with most of the flesh makes the bird a נבלה, the bird is already 'dead' at that point. So cutting the סימנים afterwards seems pointless.

keyTerms.term: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
keyTerms.meaning: If something is difficult for me, this is what is difficult for me
A dead animal or bird
Pinches; does מליקה, the way a bird offering is killed with the fingernail from the back of the neck

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying מליקה is invalid. He is asking what the extra pinching of the סימנים adds, since the bird seems to be considered dead already.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי,
phrases.english: If something is difficult for me, this is difficult for me:
And does he stand and pinch a dead bird?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַשְׁיָא לִי הָא קַשְׁיָא לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב חסדא's proof for זעירי is rejected, רבא returns to זעירי's ruling from step 7 and raises his own difficulty against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: זעירי's ruling that a broken neck bone with most of the flesh makes the bird a נבלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In מליקה the bone and most of the flesh are cut before the סימנים. By זעירי's rule the bird would already be a נבלה at that point, so the rest of the pinching could not make it fit. Since מליקה clearly works, זעירי's rule seems wrong.

steps.title: אביי shows the same problem in a bird עולה
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that even without that ruling, a bird עולה has the same problem: it needs both סימנים cut, but after one סימן the bird already counts as dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Then let the bird burnt offering also be difficult for you, since it needs two סימנים cut. And does he stand and pinch a dead bird?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells רבא that his question is even bigger than he thinks. The same problem shows up in the עולת העוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For an ordinary bird, cutting one סימן is enough to count as killed. Yet an עולת העוף requires cutting both סימנים, which means the כהן keeps pinching after the bird is already considered dead. So the question does not depend on the neck-bone ruling at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A bird brought as a burnt offering
Both signs: the windpipe and the food pipe
Then let it be difficult for you as well

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Then let the bird burnt offering be difficult for you,
since it requires two simanim,
and does he stand and pinch a dead bird?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Widens רבא's question by showing it also applies to a bird עולה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's challenge to זעירי. אביי argues that it proves too much, because the same question would apply to the עולת העוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After one סימן the bird is already dead, so cutting the second seems pointless, just like רבא's case.

steps.title: רבא: the extra pinching fulfills the מצוה of הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that in the עולה case, the continued pinching is done to fulfill the מצוה of separating the head from the body.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: There, it is in order to fulfill the מצוה of separation through it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why the כהן keeps going in a bird עולה. The extra cutting has its own purpose: the מצוה of הבדלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra pinching is not meant to kill the bird, which is already done. It is done to fulfill a separate מצוה for the עולה: separating the head from the body. So it is not pointless after all.

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of separating the head from the body in a bird עולה
There, in that case

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם כְּדֵי לְקַיֵּים בָּהּ מִצְוַת הַבְדָּלָה.
phrases.english: There, it is in order to fulfill through it the מצוה of separation.
phrases.notes: 'There' means the bird עולה, where the head must be fully separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם כְּדֵי לְקַיֵּים בָּהּ מִצְוַת הַבְדָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge about the עולת העוף.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a new purpose for the extra action
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Continuing to pinch after the bird is dead is pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: In a bird עולה, the continued pinching fulfills the מצוה of הבדלה.

steps.title: Then the skin should also need cutting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if the point is to separate the head, then the skin should also have to be cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the skin should also have to be cut!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. If the goal is to separate the head, why stop at the סימנים and not cut the skin too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A real separation of the head would mean cutting through everything, skin included. Yet the הלכה only requires cutting the סימנים. This seems to show that הבדלה is not the reason after all.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Skin

phrases.english: If so, the skin as well!
phrases.notes: He means the skin should also have to be cut, so the head is truly separated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's הבדלה answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the extra pinching is for הבדלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goal is separating the head, the skin should also have to be cut, but it does not.

steps.title: Only what blocks שחיטה blocks הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: whatever invalidates שחיטה invalidates הבדלה, and what does not invalidate שחיטה, such as the skin, does not invalidate הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anything that holds back the slaughter holds back the separation, and anything that does not hold back the slaughter does not hold back the separation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question about the skin by tying the rules of הבדלה to the rules of שחיטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הבדלה follows the same boundaries as שחיטה. Leaving the skin uncut does not ruin a שחיטה, so it does not ruin the הבדלה either. That is why the skin does not need to be cut.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds back; invalidates if missing
Ritual slaughter

phrases.english: Anything that invalidates in slaughter
invalidates in separation,
and anything that does not invalidate in slaughter
does not invalidate in separation.
phrases.notes: The skin is the example here: an uncut skin does not ruin a שחיטה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the skin.
steps.terutzResolutionType: States a general rule linking הבדלה to שחיטה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הבדלה should require cutting everything, including skin.
steps.terutzMaskana: הבדלה only includes what invalidates שחיטה, and the skin does not.

steps.title: The minority of the סימנים breaks the rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: according to the רבנן, the remaining minority of the סימנים does not invalidate שחיטה, yet it does invalidate הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the minority of the סימנים, according to the Rabbis, does not invalidate slaughter, and yet it does invalidate separation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule just given by pointing to a case where it does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For שחיטה, cutting most of a סימן is enough, so a small uncut part does not ruin it. But for הבדלה, the רבנן require the סימנים to be cut fully. So something that does not block שחיטה does block הבדלה, which breaks the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The small remaining part of the סימנים
The Sages, the majority view

phrases.english: But isn't there the minority of the simanim according to the Rabbis,
which do not invalidate in slaughter,
and they do invalidate in separation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule stated in the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that only what invalidates שחיטה invalidates הבדלה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The minority of the סימנים does not invalidate שחיטה but does invalidate הבדלה, which contradicts the rule.

steps.title: Corrected rule: whatever is part of שחיטה is part of הבדלה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the rule: anything that belongs to שחיטה belongs to הבדלה, and anything that is not part of שחיטה is not part of הבדלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: Anything that is part of slaughter is part of separation, and anything that is not part of slaughter is not part of separation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of the rule so it fits both the skin and the minority of the סימנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is no longer 'does it invalidate שחיטה' but 'is it part of שחיטה at all.' The full סימנים are part of שחיטה, even if a small part left uncut does not ruin it, so they are included in הבדלה. The skin is not part of שחיטה at all, so it is not needed for הבדלה.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say; the wording is being corrected
It is included, it belongs to

steps.whatToRemember: הבדלה covers whatever belongs to שחיטה: the full סימנים are included, while the skin is not.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
Anything that is part of slaughter
is part of separation,
and anything that is not part of slaughter
is not part of separation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: כֹּל שֶׁיֶּשְׁנוֹ בִּשְׁחִיטָה יֶשְׁנוֹ בְּהַבְדָּלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rewords the rule to answer the challenge from the minority of the סימנים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule depends on what invalidates שחיטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule depends on what is part of שחיטה at all, so the full סימנים are included and the skin is not.
